title: Complaint of Devin & Tracey Ehrlich vs. North Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied the complaint that North Georgia Presbytery erred by sustaining the Session’s instruction not to distribute the open letter.
first_summary: Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, reasoning that their membership vows obliged them to obey lawful church injunctions and that circulation would disturb the church’s peace after Presbytery found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses.
summary: Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority.
